findings.claim: Hidden coupling: tests 3-7 cannot pass until task 8 is done. starter/src/dev-auth.js line 10 ships 'enabled: true', and AuthContext.jsx lines 8-10 seed the session from it, so the app starts signed in as 'Dev Admin (auto)'. Tests t3 to t7 each open a guarded route ('/admin' or '/') and first await findByRole('heading', {name: 'Sign in to Beacon'}). With auto-sign-in on, the guard always sees a user, so (reasoned from the code) that lookup times out however correct tasks 3-7 are. On the shipped starter, tests 3-8 all fail with the same 'Unable to find role="heading" and name "Sign in to Beacon"' (observed by running npm test on a copy), and the message never names dev-auth.js. The README discloses only the test 1 / task 2 coupling (lines 50-52), and line 103 states that 'Your tasks 1-3 make this flow work' for task 5, which is false while auto-sign-in is on. A learner working in task order produces five correct implementations whose tests stay red until the last task, and the failure points back at their guard.
findings.recommendation: Move 'turn off auto-sign-in' (dev-auth.js) to the start, as task 1 or part of task 3, and leave the apiUrl work in task 8. Otherwise have tests 3-7 disable devAutoSignIn themselves. In either case, disclose the remaining dependency in 'How to test' and correct README line 103.

findings.claim: The review-topic objectives are over-claimed. lab.json claims javascript-fundamentals-review#o1-o3 and react-review#o1 (lines 23-26), and the note (line 80) says they are 'exercised as scored production work across the tasks'. Both review topics record lab 'none' in their topic.json. #o3 (ES module import and export, default and named) is not practised at all: every import and export in the eight edited files ships pre-written, and no task needs a new one; NotAllowedNotice is in the same file as AdminPage. #o1 (destructuring, spread, arrow functions, map and filter): the map calls are in given code and no task needs spread, map or filter. react-review#o1 asks for components, props, state, effects, routing, forms and context on short mixed problems 'including every re-render trigger taught'; the only effect is in given code (use-authed-fetch.js), and no test scores a re-render trigger. #o1 and react-review#o1 are therefore incidental and unscored. module.json says the module lab covers 'the four S34 topics', and the review topics are S35, the day after this S34 lab.
findings.recommendation: Remove javascript-fundamentals-review#o3 from objectives. Either remove #o1 and react-review#o1 too, or add explicit partial notes naming the clauses a test actually scores. Keep #o2 (the async/await fetch trace) if wanted, since authFetch and the 401/403 catch branches genuinely score it. Then reconcile covers with the catalog: update the review topics' lab field and the module.json note, or drop the two review topics from covers.

findings.claim: Several claimed objectives are only partly practised, with no partial-objective note; the only such note covers turning-off-the-dev-profile#o2. (a) handling-401-and-403-redirect-and-sign-out#o2: the 401 clear-and-redirect loop is given code (sessionExpired in AuthContext.jsx lines 38-41, and use-authed-fetch.js). Task 5 asks for no edit, yet sits in failingTests. The one 401 branch the learner writes, handleRestart in OverviewPage.jsx line 34, is never asserted by t6. The clause about distinguishing this from the server ending an HttpOnly cookie session is absent. (b) #o1 begins 'State the general HTTP meanings of 401 and 403', which no test can score. (c) turning-off-the-dev-profile#o3 ('Verify after the switch that an unauthenticated request is now refused') is not practised: t8 only checks that the app opens on the login page, and no request is sent without a token.
findings.recommendation: Add honest partial-objective notes for handling-401#o1 and #o2 and for turning-off-the-dev-profile#o3, naming which clauses the lab scores. Better still, assert the learner-written 401 branch in handleRestart, and add a step in which the learner sends one unauthenticated authFetch and observes the 401.

findings.claim: The 25-minute median and 30-minute cap (lines 82-85) are optimistic. This is a reasoned estimate, not a measurement. The learner edits 8 files: signIn, handleSubmit with try/catch and navigation from location.state, signOut and its header wiring, authFetch, RequireSignIn with Navigate state, role-gated link and page, handleRestart with 403/401/success branches, the dev flag, and apiUrl. They must also read the given task 5 flow. edu-ar-1 adds debugging time, because five tests stay red after correct work. The accepted comparable fetch-and-browser-client lab budgets 38/45 for seven single-function tasks in one file.
findings.recommendation: Re-time after fixing edu-ar-1, and drop the read-only task 5 from the timed set if needed. Otherwise state a figure a dry run supports.

findings.claim: The setup commands do not work when run in order. The first block runs 'cd tests' (line 27), and the optional block then runs 'cd starter' (line 34), which fails from inside tests/. 'How to test' then says 'From the tests folder', while that learner is now in starter/ with the dev server occupying the terminal.
findings.recommendation: Use 'cd ../starter', or anchor both blocks at the coding-lab folder, and note that tests run in a second terminal from tests/.
